newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB says regrets Moody"s rating review.
newsitem.headline: LTCB says regrets Moody"s rating review.

text.p: The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) said on Tuesday that it regretted a move by Moody"s Investors Service to review the bank"s senior debt ratings for a possible downgrade.
The bank said in a statement that it would explain its management policy to Moody"s and seek understanding from the credit rating agency.

Moody"s said earlier on Tuesday it was reviewing the LTCB"s Baa1 senior debt rating, reflecting its concern about the impact of Japan"s accelerating shift toward less regulated financial markets on the LTCB and the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd"s (IBJ) competitive positions as long-term credit banks.
"It is regrettable that Moody's announced a review of our ratings when our earnings situation is steadily improving," the bank said in a statement.
LTCB said Moody"s might have decided on the review because it was concerned about the possible negative impact of Japan"s "Big Bang" reforms on long-term credit banks.
But the bank said it believes the reforms will provide it with far more opportunity to boost profits through investment banking operations.
It said the bank would take the opportunity to strengthen its business by shifting some of its resources to its investment banking operations.
"We will explain our management policy to Moody"s," LTCB said.
LTCB"s shares closed down 11 yen at 388 on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
